## 3. What exists in the repo (develop plus PR #53)

**Mod team (one loop, do not change it):** the user approves, then `dayz-orchestrator` (main session, `claude --agent agentic-z:dayz-orchestrator`) plans with `dayz-mod-architect`, then `dayz-lead` (one per team: script, config, art, UI, server, release) runs the specialist workers and the read-only gates (`dayz-mod-reviewer`, plus `dayz-layout-validator` for `.layout` work). The orchestrator runs `/dayz-gate build` then `/dayz-gate ingame` once per wave, one test session at a time. Known failures go straight to the owning lead with the fix; new ones go to `dayz-mod-debugger`. After the user says yes, they publish with DayZ Tools Publisher.

**Agents (22):** orchestrator, mod-architect, lead, build-checker and ingame-tester (now fallbacks for `/dayz-gate`), build-engineer (Haiku), docs-writer (Sonnet), router (Haiku), script, config, asset, object-builder, UI, map, server-admin, workbench, mod-debugger, mod-reviewer, layout-validator, figma-node-normalizer, figma-to-dayz-layout, agent-creator.

**Token-saving layer (PR #53), documented in `docs/token-saving.md`:**
1. `/dayz-gate build|ingame`: script-only checks with PASS or FAIL output.
2. `triage.py`: 24 known errors with fix and owner; `--learn` adds per-project ones.
3. `/dayz-route`: keyword rules, then Jev when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set, then the Haiku `dayz-router`.
4. Plugin hooks (`hooks/hooks.json`): a syntax check after config and layout edits, and a scope guard against other mods.
5. `/dayz-statusline`: shows P:, active mod, Diag running, index age.
6. Model pins on simple roles.
7. Tier 2 split into a core file plus `_shared/conventions/{config,assets,scripts,ui,server}.md`, 31% less rules text per run.
8. `agentic-z-panel` (Claude Code mod in `mods/agentic-z-panel`, version 0.2.0, second plugin in the marketplace): `/dayz-panel` with buttons for mount, build, check build, check in game, deploy, launch, stop, Workbench and Object Builder.
9. A `.bat` for every runnable skill (35, listed in `scripts/README.md`). Fixed `dayz-search.bat`, which crashed on start.
10. Skill and agent descriptions trimmed, saving about 2,100 tokens per session.

**Three tiers:** Tier 1 `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` (byte-identical, edit all three). Tier 2 `.claude/skills/_shared/dayz-conventions.md` plus topic files. Tier 3 agents, skills and knowledge packs. Corrections go in through `/dayz-record-correction`.

## 6. New specialists (in scope; not started)

Based on the knowledge pack handoff (`agentic-z-pack-handoff.md`). Agentic-Z stays the base, and the loop does not change. New specialists join existing leads as workers. Their `references/` folders are knowledge packs loaded only when needed. `/dayz-lint` runs inside the existing build gate.

1. **Research map**: every topic from outside research and the knowledge pack, sorted by subject. Private, never in the repo.
2. **Foundation**: client and server ownership rules in Tier 2, a `references/` layout, and an empty evals folder.
3. **`/dayz-lint`**: our own checker for boot-time errors, run inside `/dayz-gate build` and `/dayz-build-pbo`, feeding triage.
4. **dayz-persistence-specialist**: saving data, save versions, migrations, base building, pre-release data audit. Joins the script lead; the audit goes to the server lead.
5. **dayz-vehicle-specialist**: cars, boats, helicopters. Config lead.
6. **dayz-weapon-specialist**: Config lead.
7. **dayz-wearables-specialist**: clothing, characters, proxies. Art lead.
8. **dayz-animation-specialist**: model.cfg, RTM, Blender handoff. Art lead.
9. **dayz-audio-fx-specialist**: any lead.
10. **dayz-physics-specialist**: any lead.
11. **dayz-ai-specialist**: Expansion AI behavior, learned only, never copied. Script lead.
12. **Upgrades**:
    * script reference;
    * UI (Dabs, widgets);
    * texture and rvmat cookbook;
    * model and LOD rules;
    * doors in object-builder;
    * a spec step in `/dayz-init`;
    * layout preview.

**Cycle for each specialist:** research, then write our own reference, then a separate agent verifies every fact against P:, then add answer tests, then wire it in (lead table, router `rules.json` plus `dayz-router.md`, reviewer and debugger owner lists, `plugin.json`), then grade to A+, then a PR to develop, then update the guide and team PDF. In-game testing needs DayZ launched on Brian's PC: ask first.

**Spec for each specialist:** the guide's "Each specialist in detail" section (what it does, a sample request, its lead, what it hands back) and its "Specialist workflows" section (the steps every specialist, old and new, follows inside the loop). Each agent file must match both. The guide's agent, skill and grade lists already name every new item, so each one you build must keep those entries true.

**Don't take:**
* `rip-vehicle-import`;
* `dayz-pbo-reverse-engineering`;
* scraped notes and Discord dumps;
* the pack's MIT label;
* copied Expansion or VPP code;
* the AI 3D generators;
* the pack's bookkeeping system.

**Also from the pack's Later list:** the Blender tools, the 3D viewer, the p3d inspector and the model preflight. They are not in the core.

**Add-ons (the guide's "Add-ons" section):** third-party tools (Blender, AI 3D generators such as a Higgsfield integration, other MCP servers) never go in the core. They go in a separate optional plugin (working name `agentic-z-addons`), one workflow per tool, each connecting the tool at one point in the loop (usually handing a model to `dayz-object-builder`), and everything they produce passes the same gates. No add-on may unpack protected mods or debinarize models. Build this plugin only after the core is done, and only the add-ons Brian names.

## 6b. Workflows (in scope; the guide's Workflows section is the spec)

* **Behavior tests in game:**
  * A test mission that spawns an item, uses it, and writes PASS or FAIL lines to the log for `/dayz-gate ingame` to read.
  * The mod architect writes one check per feature.
  * This is the next step past "loads with clean logs".
* **Paste-in workflows:** paste one of these and the right thing happens.
  * A crash log or RPT gets triaged.
  * A screenshot finds the widget, texture or class.
  * A Figma link runs the Figma pipeline.
  * A Workshop or GitHub link gets imported.
  * A `types.xml` chunk gets checked and merged.
* **Mod recipes:** "new weapon", "new vest" and "new craftable" templates that pre-fill the architect's plan.
* **Live log watch:** during a test session, flag script errors the moment they appear.
* **Visual check:** screenshot the game at test time and compare.
* **Release pack:** Workshop description, changelog, classname list and server-owner install notes in one go.
* **Upgrade guard:** after a DayZ update, re-index, diff, and flag mod classes whose parents changed.
* **Conflict checker:** load the mod with CF, COT and Expansion and report collisions.
* **Server-owner kit:** types, cfgeconomycore lines, load order and keys, zipped.
* **Balance sheet:** compare item stats with similar vanilla items.
* **Mod health dashboard:** last build, last test, open findings and test history per mod.
* **Ask the codebase:** plain-English vanilla questions answered with `path:line` citations.
* **More savings:**
  * prompt caching for big rules files;
  * a cache of repeated RAG answers;
  * per-agent evals.
